CTGAN and CopulaGAN are the classical baselines it is measured against, so SDV defines the bar a quantum method has to clear, from an industrial chemistry lab rather than an academic group.

paper-training-free-retrieval-augmented-.summary: Proposes R2RAG-Flood, a training-free retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses a reasoning-centric knowledge base and case-based reasoning with LLM backbones to nowcast flood property damage severity, evaluated on a Hurricane Harvey case study in Harris County, Texas. The paper mentions class imbalance mitigation strategies in supervised learning, citing CTGAN as an example of conditional tabular synthesis. SDV's CTGAN is only cited in passing as prior art for handling class imbalance, not used in the proposed pipeline.
paper-training-free-retrieval-augmented-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is actually run anywhere in the pipeline or purely cited in the intro.

paper-hybrid-framework-attention-tabular.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid pavement-engineering model combining an attention-based TabNet with XGBoost boosting to predict asphalt dynamic modulus from scarce, heterogeneous datasets. To address data scarcity, it uses Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) to generate synthetic training samples, and reports that models trained on CTGAN-augmented data outperform those trained on real data alone or with alternative augmentation methods (R²=0.98). CTGAN is run as the synthetic data generator whose output drives the paper's headline predictive result.
paper-hybrid-framework-attention-tabular.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a custom reimplementation, nor whether conditional sampling specifics are discussed.

paper-addressing-environmental-challenge.summary: This paper proposes a dual-method data generation framework to augment scarce peak particle velocity (PPV) data for blast-induced ground vibration monitoring in tunneling, combining an empirical USBM-formula-based generator with a deep-learning-based Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) that learns patterns from the original dataset to produce realistic synthetic PPV records. The augmented datasets are shown to significantly improve downstream machine learning PPV predictors compared to training on raw data alone. TVAE, the SDV-family tabular synthesizer, is run as the core deep generative strategy producing the synthetic samples that the augmentation pipeline depends on.
paper-addressing-environmental-challenge.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the SDV/CTGAN package's TVAE implementation was directly invoked (api_user) or reimplemented (port).

paper-llm-framework-synthetic-generation.summary: This paper presents a proof-of-concept platform that uses fine-tuned Large Language Models combined with differential privacy techniques (IBM's diffprivlib) to generate synthetic datasets across domains including healthcare, finance, retail, logistics, and cybersecurity, positioning LLMs as more scalable and adaptable than GANs or VAEs. The related-work section briefly cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper as an example of a previous approach whose lack of versatility and privacy protection the new platform aims to address, without running or engaging further with SDV's methods.
paper-llm-framework-synthetic-generation.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliations unknown from metadata alone.

paper-dp-tabula-2025.summary: Generates differentially private tabular data by fine-tuning a language model rather than a GAN, training the foundation model under a privacy budget and sampling from it. CTGAN appears as prior art in the survey of GAN-based tabular generation the paper positions itself against.

paper-augmentation-variational-autoencod.summary: This paper proposes a novel data augmentation method for imbalanced regression (IR), combining a variational autoencoder with a smoothed bootstrap in the latent space to generate synthetic rare/extreme target values for tabular regression tasks. It benchmarks its method against several baselines including SMOTE-style resamplers and standard synthetic data generators. TVAE, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN from the SDV python package are run as baseline synthetic data generators and are found to underperform the proposed method on imbalanced regression benchmarks.

paper-driven-derive-equation-predicting-.summary: This paper develops a unified empirical equation for the ultimate shear strength of stirrup-free reinforced concrete beams, combining an experimental database with Artificial Neural Networks, Generative Adversarial Networks, and Bayesian optimization to fit and refine the formula. To expand the training data, the authors use SDV's CTGANSynthesizer to generate synthetic datasets of independent variables (concrete strength, beam dimensions) at scales up to 1,000,000 instances, which are then fed through a trained ANN to estimate corresponding shear strengths. SDV's CTGAN synthesizer is run directly as the generator underpinning the study's synthetic data augmentation pipeline.

paper-enhancing-predictive-accuracy-medi.summary: This paper compares two oversampling strategies for class-imbalanced medical data on the Pima Indians Diabetes dataset: SMOTE and the Conditional Tabular GAN (ctGAN), training a multilayer perceptron classifier on each augmented dataset and evaluating accuracy, precision, sensitivity, F1, and distributional fidelity metrics. SMOTE consistently outperformed ctGAN, though ctGAN produced higher precision and richer distributional variability. CTGAN is run directly as one of the two generative augmentation methods evaluated, with its conditional generator/discriminator formalism described and its hyperparameters specified for reproducibility.
paper-enhancing-predictive-accuracy-medi.needs: Evidence describes ctGAN's architecture and hyperparameters in detail but never names the sdv-dev/CTGAN package explicitly; assumed to be the standard SDV-family CTGAN implementation given the parameter description and citation to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper.

paper-evaluating-bimodal-user-verificati.summary: This paper designs a bimodal smartphone user-verification system that fuses behavioral (pickup gesture) and biological (face) biometrics, and tests its robustness against four distinct synthetic-data attack scenarios. One of these attacks uses generated tabular data to mimic a user's pickup-gesture signal, evaluated via t-SNE and KL-divergence comparisons against genuine data. CTGAN is run to synthesize the fake pickup-gesture data used as one of the four attack vectors probing the verification model's robustness.

paper-generating-synthetic-relational-ta.summary: This paper proposes a framework that extends TabPFN's structural-causal-model (SCM) approach for generating synthetic single-table data to relational, multi-table settings, producing synthetic tables connected via shared key columns with realistic inter- and intra-table dependencies. The framework samples DAG structures and propagates data through structural assignments, targeting use cases like foundation model training and benchmark creation. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited in related work as the first learning-based approach for generating relational data, but it is not run or compared against in the experiments.

paper-llm-synthetic-tabular-generation-2.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage pipeline combining large language model-based synthetic tabular data generation with an automated curation step that balances privacy and utility for privacy-sensitive scientific domains such as medicine and social sciences. It evaluates LLMs of varying scale against a battery of specialized generative baselines, finding LLMs superior in statistical fidelity and downstream utility but with greater privacy risk, which the curation pipeline partially mitigates. CTGAN is included as one of roughly a dozen specialized baseline models (alongside PATEGAN, ADSGAN, TVAE, RTVAE, diffusion and probabilistic-graph models) trained and scored across statistical, performance, detection and privacy metrics.
paper-llm-synthetic-tabular-generation-2.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package directly or via the Synthcity library (also cited, [24]) which bundles similar generators; the paper frames Synthcity as only a metrics suite but does not clarify the source of the generator implementations.

paper-leveraging-social-determinants-hea.summary: This paper builds a knowledge graph framework linking Social Determinants of Health to mental health outcomes in veterans with suicide risk, using electronic health records from the U.S. Veterans Health Administration, and applies link prediction and node classification to uncover latent patterns while generating synthetic data to preserve privacy. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is only cited in the reference list as prior work on synthetic data generation, with no evidence it was run in this study.
paper-leveraging-social-determinants-hea.needs: The paper mentions generating synthetic data preserving statistical properties but does not name the tool used; SDV citation appears bibliography-only, so it cannot be confirmed SDV software was run.

paper-machine-learning-prediction-carbon.summary: This paper develops five machine learning models, centered on a physics-informed artificial neural network with a symbolic formula and dropout layer, to predict carbonation depth in alkali-activated materials from CO2 concentration, CaO/MgO content and other governing factors. SHAP analysis is used to interpret contributions of these factors to carbonation resistance. CTGAN is employed as a data augmentation technique to enlarge the training set, but is found less effective than the proposed physics-informed model, with compromised prediction accuracy and generalization.
paper-machine-learning-prediction-carbon.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented, nor its exact role (data augmentation vs. comparison model) beyond what the abstract states.

paper-magnitude-impact-hallucinations-ta.summary: This validation study examines 'hallucinations'—synthetic records not present in the source population—across 6354 training datasets derived from 12 large real-world healthcare datasets, generated with seven synthetic data generation (SDG) models. It measures how hallucination rate scales with training data complexity and whether it degrades downstream prognostic machine learning performance (LightGBM, MLP), finding hallucinations are common but rarely impair utility. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of the seven SDG models benchmarked in the empirical evaluation.
paper-magnitude-impact-hallucinations-ta.needs: Author affiliations not printed in the extracted text (only numeric superscripts), so left null.

paper-microstructural-assessment-supervi.summary: This study develops machine-learning models (XGBoost, CatBoost, gradient boosting, etc.) to predict the compressive strength of quartz-powder and fly-ash blended concrete, combining experimental testing, microstructural analysis, and SHAP-based feature importance. The abstract and available evidence do not describe how CTGAN is used, but the paper's reference list cites the CTGAN paper, suggesting it may have been used to augment a limited experimental dataset for model training, though this cannot be confirmed from the given evidence.
paper-microstructural-assessment-supervi.needs: No full text or citing sentence provided; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run (e.g., for data augmentation of the small concrete dataset) or merely cited in passing.

paper-prediction-forming-accuracy-proces.summary: This manufacturing engineering paper proposes a hybrid CTGAN-DBN-NSGA-II framework for predicting axial and radial forming accuracy in Static Pressure Support-Single Point Incremental Forming (SPS-SPIF), using CTGAN to augment a small experimental dataset, a Deep Belief Network to model the parameter-accuracy relationship, and NSGA-II for multi-objective process optimization. The generated data's fidelity is validated using KL divergence and SDMetrics' coverage quality evaluation against SMOTE and VAE baselines. CTGAN is run as the core data-augmentation generator underpinning the entire empirical pipeline, and SDMetrics is used directly to evaluate the synthetic data's distributional quality.
paper-prediction-forming-accuracy-proces.needs: CTGAN itself is cited (mis-attributed to 'Lei et al.') rather than named as a package import; hyperparameter table names differ slightly from standard sdv-dev CTGAN constructor args, but explicit use of SDMetrics as a named toolkit supports api_user integration.

paper-synthetic-operational-generation-d.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid PCA-CTGAN method for generating synthetic operational data for deep-learning-based power transmission line fault protection, where PCA reduces the dimensionality of high-frequency time-series data before CTGAN synthesizes samples. The synthetic data is used to augment a small real dataset, improving an LSTM fault-classification model's accuracy from 50.93% to 86.07%, with additional validation on sub-synchronous oscillation data. CTGAN's conditional generator, mode-specific normalization, and training-by-sampling techniques are described and used as the generative engine driving the entire empirical programme, though no library implementation details (package name, hyperparameters) are given.
paper-synthetic-operational-generation-d.needs: No package name, import, or hyperparameter table is given, so it is unclear whether the authors ran the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation or built their own from the paper's description; integration marked unclear pending that detail.

paper-wearable-physical-activity-timeser.summary: Generates 100 synthetic wearable users from 100 real ones, keeping the multivariate time-series structure — datetime, numeric and categorical columns together — and reports KS 0.014, Jensen-Shannon 0.057 and pairwise correlation 0.011 against the real data. The two generators are PAR and CTGAN and the metrics are the KSComplement/pairwise-correlation set; that combination exists as a pair only in SDV's sequential and single-table APIs, but no library is named, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.
paper-wearable-physical-activity-timeser.needs: IEEE Xplore is paywalled to automated fetches. PAR alongside CTGAN and those three metrics points to SDV's PARSynthesizer and SDMetrics, but that inference needs the methods section before integration moves off unclear.

paper-synthetic-generation-health-demogr.summary: This study evaluates three open-source generative models—CTGAN, TableGAN, and CopulaGAN—for producing synthetic tabular data from a Health and Demographic Surveillance System dataset in rural Kenya, assessing fidelity, utility, and privacy to gauge feasibility of synthetic data sharing in low- and middle-income countries. CTGAN produced the highest-fidelity synthetic data and preserved utility for downstream Random Forest classification comparably to real data, while CopulaGAN performed moderately and TableGAN failed outright. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN synthesizers (the latter documented via docs.sdv.dev) are run directly as the generative models under comparison, with CTGAN's output driving the paper's headline results.
paper-synthetic-generation-health-demogr.needs: Full affiliations for authors beyond the first three (Rego, Weinheimer-Haus, Alarakhiya, Ngugi, Price, Zhu, Wong, Siwo) were not visible in the provided evidence.

paper-comprehensive-review-generative-ed.summary: This is a broad survey of generative AI (GAI) technologies and their applications, benefits, and challenges within education, covering content generation, adaptive learning, conversational systems, and issues like privacy and bias. It is a review paper synthesizing prior literature rather than presenting new experiments. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing as an example supporting the claim that AI-generated synthetic datasets can serve as safe, trustworthy training tools.
paper-comprehensive-review-generative-ed.needs: Full text not available; only an abstract and a single citing sentence were seen, so the depth of engagement with SDV beyond a passing citation cannot be confirmed.

paper-menstrual-cycle-prediction-gan-202.summary: This conference paper predicts menstrual cycle regularity and cycle length by combining TabNet with GAN-generated synthetic data to overcome the low observation-to-variable ratio and class imbalance typical of menstrual cycle datasets. TabNet paired with CTGAN-generated data outperformed Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LSTM baselines (also paired with CTGAN) on classification, and was competitive on regression. CTGAN is run directly as the synthetic data generator underlying every model's training pipeline, with its conditional vector and mode-specific normalization described as the mechanism for addressing class imbalance.
paper-menstrual-cycle-prediction-gan-202.needs: Not explicit whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent CTGAN implementation was used; treated as api_user given detailed description of the standard CTGAN mechanism (conditional vector, mode-specific normalization) without evidence of reimplementation.

paper-enhanced-prediction-long-term-2024.summary: This study builds machine-learning models (random forest, SARIMA, LSTM) to predict long-term bottom dissolved oxygen concentration in Masan Bay, Korea, using combined water-quality, meteorological, and river/discharge monitoring records, with wavelet-based feature selection to handle non-stationarity. To address the limited and irregular observation data, the authors used a neural-network-based data synthesis method to augment their dataset before model training. The data-synthesis augmentation step cites the original SDV framework, run to expand the training data rather than as the paper's main contribution.
paper-enhanced-prediction-long-term-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether the authors ran the actual SDV/CTGAN software or a custom neural-network synthesis approach only inspired by it.

paper-ganct-covid-2024.summary: Augments a COVID-19 patient dataset so classifiers have enough records to train on, then measures the predictions against the real data. GANCT extends CTGAN with customisations for the clinical variables and was trained for 3000 epochs on a V100.

paper-anonymize-synthesize-privacy-prese.summary: This study evaluates anonymization (via the ARX tool) and data synthetization (via the authors' ASyH pipeline) for protecting patient privacy in a real-world cardiology dataset, assessing utility through heart failure risk scores and residual re-identification risk. The ASyH pipeline trains four SDV synthesizers -- Gaussian copula, TVAE, CTGAN, and Gaussian copula GAN -- on the original data and selects the best-performing one using SDMetrics' Quality Report fidelity score. SDV's synthesizer suite and SDMetrics' quality report are run as the core generation and evaluation engine underlying the paper's synthetic data results.

paper-boarding-iss-imbalanced-self-2024.summary: This paper studies imbalanced self-supervised learning for mixed tabular data, focusing on autoencoders, and proposes a novel Multi-Supervised Balanced MSE loss to counter the distortions standard MSE/cross-entropy causes when categorical variables are imbalanced. The method is validated through simulations and multiple real datasets across supervised, unsupervised and generative settings. In its related-work discussion the paper cites Xu et al. (2019), noting that they adapted a VAE for mixed tabular data generation (TVAE) and proposed a conditional GAN (CTGAN) for synthetic data generation, without running either model.

paper-enhancing-resilience-edge-iot-2024.summary: This article proposes an Adversarial-Aware Data (AAD) framework that trains edge-IoT intrusion-detection models to be robust against unknown adversarial attacks, using a new generator called SE-GAN to synthesize adversarial training samples. SE-GAN is explicitly built as a self-attention variant of CTGAN, and the authors also run plain CTGAN as a comparison baseline across UNSW-15, Power System, and TON-IoT datasets. SDV's CTGAN architecture and its conditional generative design are modified into this new self-attention model, making CTGAN both the architectural foundation of the proposed method and one of the baselines it is benchmarked against.
paper-enhancing-resilience-edge-iot-2024.needs: Unclear whether SE-GAN and the CTGAN baseline were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or a from-scratch reimplementation; text gives no import or library name, only architectural description.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ov.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based approach to address overlapped and imbalanced class distributions in a structural impact damage classification task, likely generating synthetic minority-class samples to improve classifier performance. The specific architecture and experimental setup are not available in the evidence obtained. CTGAN is cited from its NeurIPS 2019 paper, but whether it is run, adapted, or only referenced as related work cannot be confirmed from the metadata alone.

paper-imb-findiff-conditional-diffusion-.summary: This paper proposes Imb-FinDiff, a denoising diffusion probabilistic model for financial tabular data that addresses class imbalance via a dual learning objective combining diffusion timestep noise prediction and class label prediction, evaluated on real-world financial datasets for downstream classifier utility and fidelity. In its related-work discussion of GAN-based approaches to mixed-type tabular data, the paper cites CTGAN as the conditional generator introduced by Xu et al. that handles mixed data types, without running or extending it.

paper-real-time-decision-support-2024.summary: This paper presents a real-time, explainable Decision Support System (DSS) for railway traffic controllers, combining linear, tree-based, and deep-learning models with SHAP explainability and agreement-level metrics, piloted at a Belgian railway infrastructure company. The abstract and citing context give no indication that synthetic tabular data generation is part of the DSS pipeline; CTGAN appears only as a cited machine-learning reference. CTGAN is mentioned only in the reference list with no described role in the study's methodology.

paper-simdiff-modeling-generation-stocha.summary: This paper proposes SimDiff, a denoising diffusion probability model for automatically learning and sampling stochastic discrete-event simulation input distributions, plus an extension SimDiff-ConvTrans for non-i.i.d. temporal inputs, and evaluates both on synthetic and real-world (emergency call center) datasets. Its evaluation protocol adopts the SDMetrics/SDV quality metrics KSComplement and Column Pair Trends, and it benchmarks its diffusion model against a Gaussian Copula baseline attributed to the SDV paper alongside CTGAN and TVAE baselines. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer and its associated fidelity metrics are run as a comparison baseline and evaluation framework, not as the proposed generator.
paper-simdiff-modeling-generation-stocha.needs: CTGAN and TVAE baselines are attributed to non-SDV papers (Zhao et al. 2021; Liu et al. 2022), so it is unclear whether they were run via the sdv-dev library or reimplemented; only the Gaussian Copula baseline and the KSComplement/Column Pair Trends metrics are explicitly tied to the SDV paper.

paper-soybean-yield-prediction-machine-2.summary: This paper conducts a secondary analysis of an agronomic field-trial dataset on cover-crop management in soybeans, comparing random forest regression to standard linear regression for yield prediction and reporting optimal hyperparameters and data-size thresholds. The abstract and available evidence give no detail on how the SDV-family paper is used, only that the original Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited. SDV is cited only in the reference list with no described role in the modeling pipeline.
paper-soybean-yield-prediction-machine-2.needs: No citing sentence or full text was available; the abstract does not mention synthetic data at all, so the role of the SDV citation (e.g., data augmentation for small agronomic datasets) is inferred, not confirmed.

paper-polish-financial-synthetic-2024.summary: Tests whether synthetic company financials retain enough statistical structure to substitute for the real filings in downstream analysis. CTGAN and TVAE generate the substitute, so SDV's two deep synthesizers stand behind a national corporate dataset.

paper-democratize-research-sensitive-sho.summary: This is an opinion/perspective article arguing that widespread adoption of synthetic data for sensitive research data has stalled, and that the data science community should shift focus from high-fidelity synthesis methods toward accessible, low-fidelity synthetic data that still supports findability, reproducibility, education, and initial research steps. The author, a data science team lead at a Dutch social science data infrastructure, proposes this reorientation rather than a new technical method. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited only in passing, in a list of tools attempting high-fidelity privacy-preserving synthesis, without being run or engaged with further.

paper-arfpy-python-package-density-2024.summary: This software paper introduces arfpy, a Python implementation of Adversarial Random Forests (ARF) for density estimation and generative modeling of tabular data, positioned as a lightweight alternative to deep-learning generators such as GANs, VAEs, normalizing flows and diffusion models. The paper contributes the arfpy package itself, inspired by an existing R implementation, with no experiments running CTGAN. CTGAN is only cited in the introduction's list of GAN-based generative modeling approaches and in the reference list, never run or compared against.

paper-credit-loan-vae-ctgan-2023.summary: Compares generation approaches on credit loan offer data, driven by the strict privacy regulation and class balance requirements that constrain financial modelling. CTGAN is one of the two models under test, so SDV's conditional generator is measured against a plain autoencoder on regulated financial records.

paper-improved-method-generating-virtual.summary: This paper proposes SSF-VSG, a virtual sample generation method for small-sample industrial datasets that combines Singular Value Decomposition for sample-space expansion with an enhanced FastMCD algorithm for outlier detection and weighted interpolation, validated on a spray painting process dataset for coating thickness prediction. The method is compared against several baseline sample-generation techniques including MCMC, SMOGN, kNN-MTD, CTGAN and WGAN in terms of MAE, MSE and MAPE. CTGAN is run as one of the comparison baselines for generating virtual training samples, not as part of the proposed method.
paper-improved-method-generating-virtual.needs: Not stated whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation was used; no hyperparameters or library name given.

paper-generation-filtered-vae-preoperati.summary: This paper proposes Filtered β-VAE, a two-stage filtered variational autoencoder that generates synthetic minority-class patient data to improve preoperative prediction of postoperative adverse events, evaluated on data from a Japanese hospital and shown to raise recall by 5.6% over prior methods. The authors compare their method against no-generation, SMOTE, and CTGAN baselines across multiple classifiers (SVM, XGBoost, logistic regression, random forest). CTGAN, described as an extension of GAN for table data, is run as one of several comparison generators for minority-class oversampling throughout the empirical evaluation.
paper-generation-filtered-vae-preoperati.needs: Evidence does not specify whether the authors used the official CTGAN package/library or their own reimplementation; no constructor parameters or library citation are given.

paper-deep-learning-prediction-models-20.summary: A systematic review synthesizing 63 studies (2016-2022) that apply deep learning to electronic health record (EHR) trajectories for clinical prediction tasks, cataloguing modeling approaches and challenges such as complex data dependencies, data insufficiency, and explainability. As part of its survey of solutions to data insufficiency, the review cites the TGAN paper on synthetic tabular data generation as related prior work, without running it.

paper-exploring-privacy-preserving-techn.summary: This paper studies model inversion attribute inference attacks against a 'propensity-to-move' machine learning model that a governmental statistical institute might release externally, proposing a two-step approach of first synthesizing training data and then applying privacy-preserving perturbations rather than combining both in one step. It compares CART-based synthesis against CTGAN and a differentially private variant (DPCTGAN) as data generation methods, then evaluates classifier utility and attack success under swapping, conditional swapping, PRAM, and differential privacy. CTGAN, run via the open-source SDV toolkit with tuned batch size, epochs, generator and discriminator dimensions, is used as one of several synthetic data generators evaluated against CART-based synthesis.
paper-exploring-privacy-preserving-techn.needs: Full text and abstract not obtained; cannot verify whether SDV software was run, adopted, or merely cited in the reference list.

paper-flood-vulnerability-oha-river-2023.summary: This paper conducts a flood vulnerability assessment of the Oha River basin in Southwestern Nigeria, using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (via an indigenous software, SAVEMACE) combined with GIS to map spatial factors such as elevation, slope, rainfall, land use, and soil, producing a flood vulnerability rating map. The abstract shows no engagement with synthetic data generation methods, and SDV/CTGAN appear only in the citation list without any evident connection to the study's hydrological modelling content.
paper-flood-vulnerability-oha-river-2023.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm context or purpose of the SDV/CTGAN citation, which appears entirely unrelated to the flood modelling topic.

paper-rfgannet-efficient-rainfall-predic.summary: RfGanNet is a rainfall-prediction pipeline for India that combines a proposed GAN-based model (RfGan) with deep convolutional neural networks to forecast rainfall across clustered regions. The paper's own text was not available, so the nature of its rainfall-generation architecture and how closely it follows prior GAN work cannot be verified beyond the citation record. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears in the reference list, suggesting it is cited as related prior GAN-based sequential/tabular data-generation work rather than demonstrably run or extended.
paper-rfgannet-efficient-rainfall-predic.needs: Full text, abstract, and citing sentence were not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is merely cited as related work or engaged with more substantively (e.g., architectural inspiration for RfGan).

paper-body-weight-lifelog-outliers-2022.summary: This paper proposes a new outlier-generation method for wearable-device body-weight lifelogs that reflects the low volatility and periodicity of weight data, aiming to correct the severe class imbalance between normal and outlier readings. The authors compare their method against SMOTE, SMOTE+ENN, SMOTE+TOMEK, and CTGAN as data-augmentation baselines, evaluating classification performance (F1, AUC) with SVM, XGBoost, and CatBoost. CTGAN's conditional-GAN/tabular-GAN design and its Variational Gaussian Mixture mode-specific normalization are described and it is run as one of several comparison methods, with the paper's own proposed algorithm reported as outperforming it.
paper-body-weight-lifelog-outliers-2022.needs: No explicit mention of the sdv-dev/ctgan package name or import; unclear whether authors used the official CTGAN library or a reimplementation, though the description matches the original algorithm closely.

paper-aim-2022.summary: AIM is a workload-adaptive algorithm for differentially private synthetic data generation that selects queries, privately measures them, and generates synthetic data from the noisy measurements, with analytic error bounds for the resulting estimates. The paper situates its contribution against prior differentially-private synthetic data mechanisms such as PrivBayes. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, as an existing algorithm noted to outperform PrivBayes on most datasets in another study's comparison, and is not run or evaluated in this paper.
paper-aim-2022.needs: Full text not obtained; only the abstract and one citing sentence were available, so it is unclear whether CTGAN is discussed further or run experimentally elsewhere in the paper.

paper-adversarial-autoencoder-generative.summary: This paper proposes SAAE, a semi-supervised intrusion detection model combining Adversarial Autoencoder and GAN architectures to reduce reliance on labeled attack data, evaluated on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and NF-UNSW-NB15. It shows the approach outperforms conventional ML methods even with only 1% labeled data. In one experimental scenario, CTGAN is run via the sdv library with default architecture to augment attack data (generating ~1800 additional samples) to retrain and improve the SAAE detector.
paper-adversarial-autoencoder-generative.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a custom implementation, and how central its output was to final results.

paper-adversarial-intrusion-detection-hy.summary: This paper proposes an intrusion-detection system for zero-day attacks that combines an LSTM-CNN hybrid deep learning classifier with generative adversarial data augmentation and an explainable-AI feature-ranking stage, tested on the AWID dataset plus simulated zero-day traffic. A generative model the authors label "TGAN" is used within their pipeline to synthesize additional attack samples for the top-ranked features. Xu and Veeramachaneni's SDV-family TGAN paper on synthesizing tabular data with GANs is cited only as the source description of the TGAN technique, with no evidence in the body text that the sdv-dev TGAN package or code was actually run.

paper-anomaly-detection-time-series-2022.summary: This paper proposes a data-centric approach for detecting anomalies in time-series data, contrasting it with model-centric neural-network tuning, and shows on a case involving memory utilization of mobile devices that correcting/augmenting the input data achieves perfect anomaly detection versus underperforming model-centric baselines. In describing its synthetic data generation for this time-series use case, it cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper as the source of the synthetic data generation concept, without describing any SDV software being run.
paper-anomaly-detection-time-series-2022.needs: No direct evidence the SDV library or a named synthesizer was actually run; the citation appears to credit SDV for the concept of synthetic time-series generation only.

paper-application-tabular-synthesis-gene.summary: This paper explores generative-adversarial-network-based synthesis of tabular data to expand small experimental datasets for machine-learning models predicting multiaxial fatigue life in materials. The synthetic data are intended to augment limited fatigue test data used to train the predictive ML models. The work cites the TGAN paper as the basis for the GAN-based tabular data synthesis approach it applies.
paper-application-tabular-synthesis-gene.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether TGAN code was actually run (api_user/port) or only cited as prior work (citation_only). Title suggests it is central to the method, but this cannot be verified from metadata alone.

paper-alfalfa-biomass-synthesis-2022.summary: Addresses the problem that a farm has too few local observations to train a yield model, and that training on non-local data from other states works no better than the scarce local data. The proposed pipeline, synthesized non-local training, fits a generator to abundant non-local records, samples a large synthetic training set from it, and classifies local yields with the result, gaining 42.9 percent accuracy over the best local or non-local baseline and topping out at 85.7 percent with a decision tree. The generators are CTGAN and TVAE taken from Xu et al., described in the paper by their mode-specific normalization and their conditional generator with training-by-sampling, and the two are compared throughout: CTGAN wins the headline result while TVAE is stronger when paired with gradient boosting. SDV's synthesizers are therefore the engine of the contribution rather than a comparison point.

paper-family-classification-malicious-ap.summary: This paper presents a computationally economical machine learning pipeline for Android malware detection and family classification, combining static, dynamic, and hybrid analysis with data sampling and feature selection techniques evaluated across multiple ML classifiers. The proposed system reports high Matthews correlation coefficients for malware detection, category classification, and family classification tasks. The TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears only in the reference list with no in-text engagement found in the full text.
paper-family-classification-malicious-ap.needs: No in-text citation sentence for reference [25] was found; classified as a bibliography-only mention.

paper-learning-fair-representation-distr.summary: This KDD 2022 paper proposes FarconVAE, a variational autoencoder that disentangles latent representations into sensitive and non-sensitive parts using a distributional contrastive loss and swap-reconstruction loss, aiming to improve fairness, model debiasing, and domain generalization across tabular, image, and text modalities. The CTGAN paper is cited only in passing as an example of neural-network success in the tabular data domain, not used or evaluated in the work.

paper-coherent-set-combining-patient-202.summary: This paper presents the Coherent Data Set, a synthetic longitudinal electronic health record combining structured patient data generated with Synthea with familial genomes, MRI DICOM images, clinical notes, and physiological time series linked via HL7 FHIR, intended for health IT and interoperability research without the privacy risks of real patient data. It is a data/methods contribution from MITRE describing a novel multimodal synthetic EHR generation pipeline rather than an evaluation of existing synthesizers. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is cited only in a list of related synthetic health-data generation approaches, with no evidence it was run or its outputs used.

paper-utility-privacy-assessment-synthet.summary: This paper empirically evaluates two open-source synthetic data generation tools, the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) and synthpop, on several publicly available human microbiome datasets, assessing both machine-learning utility and privacy risk (via nearest-neighbor distance to original samples). The authors find both tools yield synthetic data with ML performance close to the original, but SDV's synthetic samples show larger minimal distances to real records, suggesting lower re-identification risk than synthpop. SDV's GaussianCopula model is run directly (via the reticulate Python interface) as one of the two synthesizers whose output forms the entire empirical comparison.
paper-utility-privacy-assessment-synthet.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; only metadata with a bare citation link to the SDV 2016 paper is available, so the nature and depth of SDV's involvement (citation only vs. actual use) cannot be verified.

paper-dark-art-machine-learning-2021.summary: This book chapter, part of a monograph on AI and automation, examines the machine learning labour process through interviews and Marxist labour-process theory, covering data processing, model building and deployment stages. In discussing synthetic data as a data-processing technique, it cites the Synthetic Data Vault paper's finding that models trained on synthetic data show 'no significant difference' in performance versus real data. The SDV paper is cited only as a supporting reference for this claim, not engaged with further or run.
paper-dark-art-machine-learning-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm how or why SDV is cited, or whether it is discussed beyond a passing reference.

paper-internet-things-iots-security-2021.summary: This paper proposes a custom deep neural network for intrusion detection in IoT networks, aiming to classify multiple types of network attacks with high accuracy and F1-score using a test-bed dataset, addressing the limitation of prior models that succeed on single attack types but fail on multi-attack detection. The abstract and metadata give no detail on how CTGAN is used, only that it is cited among the paper's references.

paper-model-counterfactual-synthesizer-i.summary: This paper proposes a Model-based Counterfactual Synthesizer (MCS), a conditional-GAN-based framework that generates counterfactual explanations for machine learning model predictions, using umbrella sampling and causal-dependence modeling to better approximate rare counterfactual queries. It evaluates variants including one trained with a 'logarithm frequency curve' sampling technique for rare/tail values, attributed to the CTGAN paper. CTGAN is only cited for this sampling idea, adopted conceptually into the authors' own synthesizer rather than run as SDV code.
paper-model-counterfactual-synthesizer-i.needs: The whole text was searched and no SDV-family term appears outside this citation and the reference list, confirming CTGAN's sampling idea is described/adapted in prose rather than the library being run.

paper-syngen-synthetic-generation-2021.summary: This work presents SynGen, a platform that generates synthetic datasets based on user requirements and available computing resources, combining the open-source Faker library with a Gaussian copula method, and allows users to run and compare machine learning algorithms on either the generated or a predefined dataset. The paper's core contribution is a user-facing synthetic data generation tool aimed at privacy preservation, system testing, and creation of ML training data. SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer is cited and used as the statistical generation method underlying the platform's synthetic tabular data output.

paper-when-machine-learning-meets-2021.summary: A comprehensive survey categorizing the interactions between privacy and machine learning into private machine learning, ML-aided privacy protection, and ML-based privacy attacks and defenses, reviewing progress and open challenges in each. It briefly cites prior work on deep generative models for synthesizing data resembling real records. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is mentioned only in passing as an example of a deep generative model that can produce synthetic tabular data for arbitrary analysis tasks, without being run or evaluated.

paper-create-synthetic-biomedical-signal.summary: This paper proposes a bidirectional recurrent neural network (BiRNN) method for generating synthetic biomedical signals, likely for augmenting biomedical time-series data. No abstract or full text was available to confirm the paper's methodology or experiments in detail. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, apparently only in passing.

paper-detecting-word-dga-domains-2020.summary: This paper proposes an ensemble-learning approach for detecting word-list based Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) domains, using 15 lexical and network-level features combined with dimensionality reduction techniques like PCA and diffusion maps, achieving 0.9503 accuracy with C5.0. To test model robustness, the authors generate 30,000 synthetic malicious domain samples and evaluate how many are misclassified as benign. CTGAN is run as the generator producing this synthetic tabular test data, chosen explicitly over TGAN for its variational Gaussian mixture mode-specific normalization and conditional generator.
paper-detecting-word-dga-domains-2020.needs: Full text needed to determine whether CTGAN was run for data augmentation or merely cited in passing; current judgment based only on metadata linking this paper to the CTGAN citation.

paper-generation-management-training-alg.summary: This conference paper proposes generating realistic training data for coalition ISR AI systems through scenario-driven simulations that produce network, sensor, and infrastructure traces, coupled with a data curation system for managing this synthetic data. It discusses heuristic methods of composing data pieces (rescaling, positioning, overlapping) as a possible alternative source of useful training data. It cites the original SDV paper only in passing, as one of several references supporting the idea that even imperfect composed synthetic data can be useful for ML training.
paper-generation-management-training-alg.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so depth of engagement with SDV cannot be confirmed beyond a passing citation.

paper-adapcla-longtail-ehr-2026.summary: Addresses the tendency of autoregressive longitudinal electronic health record generators to underrepresent rare diagnosis codes and their co-occurrence structure, by adding a frequency-derived prior bias to the output logits as a temporary training scaffold that is annealed to zero, so the model internalizes rare-event dependencies in its own parameters instead of depending on an external correction at inference, and supports zero-shot adaptation to a population with different code frequencies through a delta-bias correction. CTGAN is present only as a bracket citation in the related work, standing in for the GAN-based tabular generators the longitudinal EHR line has moved past and, in one place, for the conditional tabular generators whose attribute conditioning the paper's zero-shot distribution control is positioned against.

preprint-augmask-training-diffusion-mode.summary: This paper proposes AugMask, a plug-and-play training framework that adapts missing-unaware diffusion backbones to incomplete tabular data by using stochastic augmentation to fill missing values as uncertain conditioning context while masking the denoising loss to only originally observed coordinates. The method is evaluated across many datasets and missingness regimes, showing that standard diffusion generators enhanced with AugMask outperform specialized missing-aware baselines. CTGAN is one of several missing-unaware generator baselines run in the experiments, explicitly using the Synthetic Data Vault's CTGAN implementation, and is also enhanced with the authors' augmentation strategy for comparison.

preprint-buddybench-privacy-constrained-.summary: BuddyBench is a benchmark linking drill-level learning trajectories, standardized clinical assessments, self-report data, and randomized-treatment endpoints from two pediatric autism/social-communication intervention cohorts, supporting knowledge tracing, next-drill recommendation, clinical prediction, and causal inference tasks. The paper also releases BuddyBench-Sim, a synthetic companion dataset intended to allow reproducible evaluation while protecting real clinical records, paired with membership-inference privacy audits. SDV and CTGAN are cited alongside TabDDPM as existing tabular data generation methods that motivate the paper's synthetic-data-plus-privacy-audit approach, but no experimental detail ties BuddyBench-Sim's generation specifically to the SDV library or CTGAN model.
preprint-buddybench-privacy-constrained-.needs: Full text does not specify which of SDV/CTGAN/TabDDPM was actually used to generate BuddyBench-Sim; the citation appears in a related-work framing rather than a methods description.

preprint-categorical-prior-lock-why-2026.summary: This paper studies why in-context learning with large language models fails to reproduce categorical distributions in structured/tabular data generation, identifying a failure mode called 'categorical prior lock-in' where LLMs cannot update pre-trained token priors even when conditioned on new examples. It contrasts this with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA), which fixes the distributional mismatch but introduces memorization risk. CTGAN is cited in the related-work section as the dominant pre-LLM GAN-based baseline, described for its conditional generator and mode-specific normalization but not run in the experiments.

preprint-knowledge-guided-retrieval-augm.summary: This preprint proposes a zero-shot, knowledge-guided framework in which large language models, steered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation over DSM-5 and ICD-10 clinical criteria, generate synthetic psychiatric tabular data without training on real patient records. The method is evaluated on six anxiety-related disorders and compared for fidelity and privacy against real-data-trained deep generative baselines. CTGAN and TVAE, both trained using the SDV library, are run as the state-of-the-art baselines against which the knowledge-guided LLM approach is benchmarked throughout the fidelity and privacy analyses.

preprint-logit-coordinate-generative-mod.summary: This preprint proposes a logit-coordinate representation that encodes categorical variables as smoothed natural parameters combined with transformed continuous variables, enabling Flow Matching and diffusion generative models to operate on mixed tabular data; it derives stability bounds and imbalance-aware convergence rates and demonstrates improvements over one-hot encodings on real-data benchmarks. CTGAN is cited in the related-work discussion as an early GAN-based approach that introduced conditional sampling and feature-wise (mode-specific) normalization for heterogeneous tabular data, but it is not implemented or run in the paper's experiments.

paper-secretfan-privacy-synthesis-2026.summary: Generates training and test data from a grammar specification rather than from a learned model, using a discriminator only as a constraint that grammar-produced samples must satisfy, so the generator never trains on the confidential records and the released data cannot reproduce them, and reports competitive utility and resemblance on eight datasets at a fraction of the compute a GAN needs. CTGAN is the prior art the design departs from: the paper describes its conditional generator and training-by-sampling as pushing resemblance so far that the model approaches a copy of the original data, leaving it exposed to membership inference, and notes that adding differential privacy to CTGAN buys that back only at the cost of utility.

preprint-tabkd-tabular-knowledge-distill.summary: This paper proposes TabKD, a data-free knowledge distillation method for tabular models that learns adaptive feature bins aligned with teacher decision boundaries and generates synthetic queries maximizing pairwise interaction coverage, outperforming five state-of-the-art extraction baselines across four datasets and teacher architectures. In its related-work section on tabular data synthesis, the paper describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generators as prior art it contrasts against, without running it. CTGAN is only cited and described, not used, in this work.

preprint-agentctg-harnessing-multi-agent.summary: This paper proposes AgentCTG, a multi-agent LLM framework for fine-grained controlled text generation, introducing agent collaboration, auto-prompting, and reflection mechanisms, and demonstrates it on tasks including toxicity mitigation, sentiment transformation, and a new Character-Driven Rewriting task for online navigation role-play. The work is about controlled natural-language generation with LLM agents and has no discernible connection to tabular synthetic data. The metadata lists a citation to the CTGAN paper, but no SDV-family mention appears anywhere in the extracted full text, suggesting a mis-attributed or lost citation rather than any actual use of CTGAN.
preprint-agentctg-harnessing-multi-agent.needs: The citation to ctgan-neurips-2019 in the metadata cannot be located in the full text; this is likely a mis-attributed or lost reference and the entry may not belong in the index at all.

preprint-biasguard-guardrailing-fairness.summary: This paper proposes BiasGuard, a post-processing fairness guardrail for deployed ML systems that uses Test-Time Augmentation to generate synthetic samples with inverted protected-attribute values, then aggregates predictions on original and augmented instances to reduce bias without retraining. Experiments across legal, medical, recruitment, and census datasets show fairness gains with minimal accuracy loss, outperforming existing post-processing baselines. The entire augmentation pipeline runs on the 'Synthetic Data Vault Project' (SDV) CTGAN implementation, explicitly tuned with its embedding_dim, generator_dim, discriminator_dim, and learning-rate hyperparameters, making CTGAN's mode-specific normalization the load-bearing generative mechanism of the method.

paper-diffusion-flow-tabular-survey-2025.summary: Surveys diffusion and flow-matching models for tabular data across seven task families - single-table synthesis, multi-relational synthesis, missing-value imputation, trustworthy and privacy-preserving generation, and anomaly detection - setting out a problem definition per family, a taxonomy of design choices over encoding, data-space versus latent-space generation and dependency handling, and comparative analyses of what each group of methods actually isolates. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE prior art the survey departs from: they are named as the earlier methods shown to achieve superior performance before diffusion, their Gaussian-mixture treatment of continuous features and one-hot handling of categoricals are the specific limitations the diffusion case is argued against, and the survey's own statement of the tabular modelling problem takes its notion of a complicated feature distribution from the CTGAN paper.

preprint-explanation-design-strategic-le.summary: This preprint studies how decision makers should design explanations for strategic agents so that agents do not respond in ways that harm their own utility, proving that action-recommendation-based explanations (ARexes) are sufficient for non-harmful responses and proposing a joint learning procedure for the predictive model and explanation policy. In their experiments on synthetic tasks, the authors fit CTGAN on an original dataset to generate additional synthetic training and testing samples used to simulate agent-DM interactions. CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, is run as the generator producing the synthetic data underlying two of the paper's experimental setups.

paper-bias-variance-ensembles-2024.summary: Decomposes the error of a model averaged over several synthetic datasets into six terms and shows that only two of them shrink as more synthetic datasets are drawn, which explains why ensembling over synthetic data helps high-variance downstream models most and lets the benefit of many datasets be predicted from a run on two. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the four generators the theory is checked against on the California housing task, run from the synthcity implementations and reported across downstream learners at one, two, five and ten synthetic datasets.

preprint-comparison-syndiffix-multi-tabl.summary: This paper compares SynDiffix, a new anonymization-focused multi-table synthetic data generator, against 15 other commercial and academic synthetic data techniques using the SDNIST analysis framework, evaluating utility and privacy across low- and high-dimensional measures. CTGAN is included as one of the 15 benchmarked techniques, credited to SDV and cited to the CTGAN paper, run as an evaluation subject rather than as the paper's own method. SDV's CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generative models compared against SynDiffix on accuracy, PCA error, and inconsistency metrics.

preprint-tabular-conditional-generative-.summary: This preprint proposes a tabular conditional generative adversarial imputation network designed for missing-data imputation in a vertical federated learning setting, where feature partitions are distributed across multiple parties. The work appears to build a GAN-based imputation architecture tailored to tabular data and federated constraints. It cites the TGAN paper as related prior work on tabular GAN design, with no evidence available on whether TGAN's code or architecture was actually run or adopted.
preprint-tabular-conditional-generative-.needs: Full text or abstract needed to confirm whether TGAN's architecture/conditional design was adopted, reimplemented, or merely cited in passing.

preprint-benchmarking-fidelity-utility-s.summary: This paper presents a benchmarking methodology and open-source tool for evaluating the fidelity and utility of synthetic relational (multi-table) data, comparing six methods including two commercial tools across several real-world relational datasets. The authors implement new fidelity metrics and utility evaluation procedures, using SDMetrics for multi-table quality assessment and the SDV metadata format for dataset specification. SDV's Gaussian-copula-based relational synthesizer is run as one of the primary methods evaluated throughout the benchmark, and SDMetrics is used and extended for quality/detection metrics.

preprint-generation-realistic-synthetic-.summary: This preprint presents a Blender-based pipeline that procedurally generates photo-realistic synthetic images of deformable cables, with randomized scene variation and physics-based draping, to train six Deep Learning image segmentation models for robotic cable perception. The work is entirely about visual/image synthetic data generation for computer vision, unrelated to tabular data. The metadata lists a citation to the original SDV (DSAA 2016) paper, but no SDV-family term or discussion appears anywhere in the retrieved full text, suggesting the citation is either peripheral or a reference-list artifact not tied to any actual use of SDV.

preprint-large-language-models-realistic.summary: This paper introduces TraceLLM, a large language model trained to recursively generate synthetic microservice call-graph traces, using instruction tuning to enforce structural constraints and capture rare cases. It demonstrates that the generated traces can replace real data for microservice management tasks like heavy-hitter prediction and anomaly detection, outperforming prior structured-data generation baselines. TVAE, the VAE-based tabular data generator introduced in the CTGAN paper, is trained as one of several baseline methods and compared against TraceLLM's recursive approach on edge-distribution similarity.

preprint-risk-calibration-generative-cla.summary: This paper proposes risk-based calibration (RC), an iterative learning procedure that refines generative classifiers (naïve Bayes, quadratic discriminant analysis) by adjusting their joint probability distributions according to 0-1 training loss rather than pure data-fitting scores, showing improved training and generalization error across 20 datasets. The work is a general contribution to supervised generative classification methodology, unrelated to synthetic tabular data generation. It cites the SDV-family vine copula paper (Sun, Cuesta-Infante, Veeramachaneni 2019) only in its reference list, with no corresponding discussion or use found in the visible body text.

preprint-textit-trans-lora-free-2024.summary: This paper proposes Trans-LoRA, a method for lossless, nearly data-free transfer of LoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning modules across base models and PEFT methods, using LLM-generated synthetic data and a discriminator-based filtering scheme rather than the original training data. The synthetic data generation itself uses large language models, not any SDV component. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in a passing list of references supporting the general claim that synthetic data is increasingly used to train machine learning models.

preprint-synthetic-generation-geometallu.summary: A preprint proposing GAN-based approaches to generate synthetic geometallurgical data, likely for use in mineral processing or ore characterization studies where real data is scarce. The metadata indicates the work cites the original TGAN (2018) paper as part of its background on GAN-based tabular data synthesis. TGAN is cited as prior work; the evidence available does not show whether it was actually run in the experiments.

preprint-evaluation-synthetic-electronic.summary: This preprint proposes two new sample-wise metrics, Similarity and Uniqueness, for evaluating synthetic tabular/EHR data beyond standard downstream-task utility measures, demonstrating them on synthetic Cystic Fibrosis patient records generated by four state-of-the-art generative models (VAE, CTGAN, and two DPGAN privacy variants). CTGAN is implemented as one of the four generators compared across utility, similarity, and uniqueness metrics, with the authors stating they 'attempted to preserve their original architecture' for each model. CTGAN's conditional-vector mechanism for handling sparse, imbalanced categorical columns is described and the model is run as one of several generators benchmarked in the study, though it appears to be the authors' own reimplementation rather than the sdv-dev package.

preprint-severity-assessment-covid-clini.summary: This medRxiv preprint develops machine learning models to predict COVID-19 severity from combined clinical features and chest CT imaging data across 346 patients from two Chinese hospitals, comparing logistic regression, neural network and gradient-boosted-tree classifiers and testing four oversampling techniques to address severe/critical case imbalance. SMOTE gave the best overall performance, though CTGAN was also tried. CTGAN, cited to the original NeurIPS 2019 conditional tabular GAN paper, was fitted on the training set and used to generate synthetic minority-class samples as one of four oversampling methods evaluated.

preprint-tabular-gans-uneven-distributio.summary: This work surveys generative approaches to tabular data synthesis and proposes an experimental pipeline that augments a training set with GAN-generated rows to counter distribution shift between train and test data, evaluating downstream classifier performance across several configurations. The later full-text version expands this into a broader survey and modular framework spanning GANs, diffusion models, and LLMs, with a 'GAN backend' implementing CTGAN-style architecture. The authors explicitly took CTGAN's published GitHub source code and, with slight modification, used it as the generator underlying their augmentation experiments, describing its mode-specific normalization and conditional-vector training-by-sampling mechanism in detail.

preprint-trustable-automated-machine-lea.summary: This preprint proposes a blockchain-based framework for trustable and automated machine learning, addressing data immutability and automation via server-layer, streaming-layer, and smart-contract implementations. It also introduces a new synthetic data generation method to enrich training data, demonstrated on fraud detection in financial data. The original SDV paper is cited only in the reference list as prior work on synthetic data generation, with no evidence it was run.

thesis-privacy-preserving-personal-analy.summary: A dissertation reporting a systematic review of 231 published works on privacy-preserving distributed data mining (PPDDM), summarizing the state of the art, comparing addressed problems, and proposing a 10-factor evaluation framework for such methods. The review appears to include CTGAN and TGAN among the many techniques surveyed as approaches relevant to privacy-preserving data analysis. No citing sentence or usage detail is available, so CTGAN/TGAN are only cited as prior work in this broad literature review.

The work is positioned within the broader literature on synthetic tabular data generation, and cites the CTGAN paper as related prior art.
